deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no computations. It is a list of research problems (Hilbert's 'problem notebook', c. 1888, judging from the cited literature). It has two entries.

ENTRY 1: hypercomplex numbers.
Reference: Dedekind, 'Zur Theorie der aus n Haupteinheiten gebildeten complexen Grössen', Göttinger Nachrichten 1885, p. 141ff. This was his reply to Weierstrass's paper of the same title (Gött. Nachr. 1884).

The setting (modern form). Take an n-dimensional commutative, associative algebra A with unit over R or C. It has basis e_1..e_n and multiplication e_i e_k = sum_l c_{ikl} e_l. Weierstrass and Dedekind show: if a certain determinant built from the structure constants does not vanish, then A is a direct sum of copies of the base field (over R: of R and C). In modern terms this is the discriminant of the trace form det(Tr(e_i e_k)), equivalently the absence of nilpotents. So such 'complex numbers' give nothing beyond ordinary ones.

Hilbert proposes three things.
(1) Extend this to infinitely many units, i.e. infinite-dimensional algebras.
(2) Extend it to quaternions, i.e. to non-commutative systems. Precisely: if only the calculational laws (multiplication table) of the quaternions hold, the units can always be replaced by actual linear substitutions. In modern language: every associative algebra with given structure constants has a faithful matrix representation. Example: i, j, k realised by 4x4 real or 2x2 complex matrices with i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1.
(3) Give a simpler proof of Dedekind's result by 'variation of the constants'. One would show that any admissible system of structure constants c_{ikl} can be deformed continuously into any other while the determinant e never vanishes. Since the conclusion is invariant along the path, it would transfer from a standard system (C^n) to all of them.

Related literature he cites: Weierstrass (1884), Hölder (Gött. Nachr. 1886, on quaternions) and Kronecker ('Zur Theorie der allgemeinen complexen Zahlen und der Modulsysteme', Berlin Sitzungsber. 1888).

My completion of the implicit idea in (3): it needs two ingredients.
- Connectedness of the locus {e ≠ 0} in the space of associative-commutative structure constants.
- Local constancy of the isomorphism type there (rigidity).
Over C both hold, because that locus is a single GL_n-orbit of C^n.
Over R the locus is disconnected: algebras R^a × C^b with different b are separated by the sign of the discriminant, (-1)^b. So the argument works over R only within each type.

ENTRY 2: intersection theorems.
The theorems named are:
- Sylvester's 'Restsatz' (residuation theorem, later the Brill–Noether Restsatz);
- Cayley's intersection theorem (Cayley–Bacharach: a cubic through 8 of the 9 base points of a pencil of cubics passes through the 9th);
- the Riemann–Roch theorem.
Hilbert proposes to reduce all of these to relations between 'characteristic functions'. Instead of speaking of common zeros (intersection points), one should speak only of the number of linearly independent conditions they impose on forms of each degree. This is exactly the programme realised in his 1890 Math. Ann. paper 'Über die Theorie der algebraischen Formen', with the characteristic function χ(m), i.e. the Hilbert function.

Example (mine). For the complete intersection Z of two plane cubics, the Hilbert function of R/(f,g) is 1, 3, 6, 8, 9, 9, … . Cubics through Z: dim = 10 − 8 = 2, so Z imposes only 8 conditions on cubics. Hence any cubic through 8 of the points is in the pencil, which is Cayley's theorem expressed purely in terms of counts of conditions.
errors: No computations, so no computational errors.

The proposed continuity proof needs more than stated. Over R the set of structure constants with e ≠ 0 is not connected: the algebras R^a × C^b lie in different components, distinguished by the sign of the discriminant. So 'from one system to all others' fails over R unless restricted to one component.
One must also show the isomorphism type is locally constant (rigidity), which the note does not address.

'Lassen sich die Einheiten immer durch wirkliche Substitutionen ersetzen' is stated as a conjecture. It is true (regular representation, already noted by Poincaré 1884 and Peirce). For quaternions specifically it was classical (Cayley 1858 matrix representation).

results.what: Program to extend Weierstrass–Dedekind theorem on commutative hypercomplex systems to infinitely many units
results.modern_name: Structure of commutative semisimple (étale) algebras; infinite-dimensional generalisation (e.g. Gelfand theory of commutative Banach algebras)
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass 1884, Dedekind 1885; later Wedderburn, Gelfand (1941) for infinite dimensions

results.what: Any system obeying the quaternion multiplication laws can be realised by actual linear substitutions
results.modern_name: Faithful (regular) matrix representation of associative algebras
results.usually_credited_to: Cayley 1858 (quaternions as matrices), Peirce 1870/81, Poincaré 1884, Study, Scheffers, Frobenius

results.what: Proof of Dedekind's theorem by continuous variation of structure constants keeping the determinant nonzero
results.modern_name: Deformation/connectedness argument; rigidity of semisimple algebras
results.usually_credited_to: Rigidity of semisimple algebras: Gerstenhaber (1964) deformation theory

results.what: Reduce Sylvester's residual theorem, Cayley's intersection theorem and Riemann–Roch to relations between characteristic functions, counting linearly independent conditions instead of intersection points
results.modern_name: Hilbert function approach to Cayley–Bacharach / residuation / Riemann–Roch
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert 1890 (characteristic function); modern Cayley–Bacharach via Hilbert functions: Eisenbud–Green–Harris 1996

deep.surprise_reason: These are research wishes, not results. The characteristic-function programme is exactly what Hilbert published in 1890, so seeing its origin here is a nice dating detail but expected. The deformation idea for Dedekind's theorem is an interesting anticipation of rigidity arguments, but it is only a sketch and incorrect as stated over R.
